title: Doubling pass of the split emitter
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number and let $w,s$ be finite Boolean words with $|s|\le |w|$. For every $j\le |s|$, after $2j$ steps the split emitter is in the configuration with control state $0$, input and counter positions both $j$, and output obtained by appending two copies of each of the first $j$ bits of $w$ to the empty word.
hypotheses_covered: The length of $s$ is at most the length of $w$
replaced:
Let the candidate's length be at most $\abs{w}$. For every $j$ at most the
candidate's length, $2j$ steps of the split emitter from its start emit each
of the first $j$ bits of $w$ twice and advance both the native head and the
candidate counter to $j$; candidate bits are read only for their presence.
